This design aims to leverage the advantages of incorporating polymers alongside inorganic thin-films to suppress diffusion pathways and to increase the lifespan of PSCs.21–23 To overcome the electrically insulating nature of polymers, the TCC incorporates highly conductive microsphere fillers protruding from a transparent polymer matrix. In effect, the in-plane conductivity of IZO and the out-of-plane conductivity of TCC work collectively to form a single encapsulating electrode (Figure 1a). We exemplify the use of this novel encapsulation scheme by benchmarking the performances of PSCs subjected to accelerated aging conditions of quasi-maximum power point (quasi-MPP) tracking under light soaking (1 sun) in air at 50˚C and 40-60% R.H. Notable improvements in operational lifetimes were observed, with a champion encapsulated PSC maintaining over 90% of its initial power conversion efficiency of 21.65% for up to 1,430 hours, compared to less than 300 hours for an unencapsulated control (Figure 1b). With a single IZO/TCC dyad, the results outperform similar work (thin- film encapsulated PSCs aged in air under illumination and MPP tracking). With the prospect of optimizing TCC characteristics (e.g., optical transparency, electrical conductivity) and architecture (e.g., number of dyads, TCO properties), our proposed innovation has the potential to facilitate advanced encapsulation strategies for the benefit of thin-film solar energy conversion devices. 2/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard Figure 1: (a) Concept image of an IZO/TCC/PSC sample. Background and Overview: Photovoltaic (PV) systems stand out among various energy resources as an attractive solution to satisfy the growing demand for electrical power. Nevertheless, reducing system costs, increasing efficiency, and extending operational lifetimes are paramount to making PV technologies more economically viable and competitive on a larger scale.24–26 Thin-film PV systems have been identified as cost- effective, high-efficiency alternatives or supplements to the energy- and material- intensive production of crystalline silicon solar cells.27,28 Among these, perovskites (e.g., organic-inorganic metal halide perovskite) are particularly notable for their rapid advancement in power conversion efficiency (PCE).29 The remarkable increase in PCE from 3.8% in 200930 to 26.7% in 202531 underscores their potential as they outpace the performance of other established thin-film PV technologies such as cadmium telluride (CdTe: PCE 23.1%) and copper indium gallium selenide (CIGSe: PCE 23.6%).31 Economically, while the 2020 benchmark on estimated minimum sustainable price (MSP)
